standard.title: Data Acquisition and Measures of Centre
standard.description: acquire data sets for discrete and continuous numerical variables and calculate the range, median, mean and mode; make and justify decisions about which measures of central tendency provide useful insights into the nature of the distribution of data
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interpret and compare distributions using mode and range (from AC9M6ST01). Students have planned and conducted statistical investigations (from AC9M6ST03).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students acquire data sets, calculate range, median, mean and mode, and justify which measure best describes a given distribution.

nodes.label: Distinguishing discrete and continuous numerical variables
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students distinguish discrete from continuous numerical variables and understand how this affects data acquisition.
nodes.minimum_width: Classify a set of variables as discrete or continuous and explain the distinction.
nodes.typical_width: Identify appropriate methods to acquire data for discrete and continuous variables; consider precision and measurement limitations for continuous data.
wider: Investigate how rounding affects continuous data: when is it appropriate to report a measurement to 1dp vs nearest integer?
Explore data acquisition from secondary sources: what are the limitations of data collected by others?

response_modes.reason: The discrete/continuous distinction is abstract until students encounter both in varied contexts. Multiple examples from different domains (counting vs measuring) are needed.

success_criteria: Correctly classifies given variables as discrete or continuous.
Explains the key distinction (countable vs measurable).
Identifies appropriate units and precision for a continuous variable.

nodes.label: Calculating range, median, mean and mode
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students calculate all four summary statistics for a given data set.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate range, median, mean and mode for a small data set with an odd number of values.
nodes.typical_width: Calculate all four statistics for data sets with even counts (median as average of two middle values); handle data sets with no mode or multiple modes.
wider: Investigate how the presence of an outlier affects each statistic differently — which is most and least sensitive to outliers?
Compare datasets with the same mean but different ranges and medians — what does each statistic reveal?

response_modes.reason: Accurate calculation of all four statistics must be fluent before comparison and justification of which is most useful. Errors in calculation undermine all subsequent reasoning.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who calculate statistics incorrectly cannot reason about which is most appropriate in Node 3 — their comparison is between wrong values, and any justification built on incorrect statistics is meaningless.
success_criteria: Correctly calculates range, median, mean and mode for a given data set.
Handles even-count data sets correctly for median.
Recognises and handles data sets with no mode or multiple modes.

nodes.label: Justifying which measure is most useful
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students reason about which measure of central tendency best describes a given distribution, considering outliers, skewness, and the purpose of the summary.
nodes.minimum_width: For a given data set, identify which measure is most useful and explain why.
nodes.typical_width: Compare two distributions using appropriate measures; explain how outliers affect the mean more than the median; choose appropriate measures for different contexts.
wider: Investigate real contexts where mean is misleading (e.g. average income with extreme wealth) and discuss which measure better represents the population.
Explore how AI systems use descriptive statistics (mean, outlier detection) — connect to practical data science.

response_modes.reason: Judgment about which statistic is most useful requires encountering distributions where each statistic tells a different story. Skewed distributions with outliers are essential test cases.

success_criteria: Identifies which measure best represents a given distribution and justifies the choice.
Explains the effect of outliers on mean vs median.
Selects different measures for different contexts appropriately.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Real-world contexts where the mean misleads (income distribution, sports statistics) offer advancing students rich critical statistical thinking — the connection to data literacy and AI applications is genuinely rich within the Year 7 band.
